title: An associate’s goal years in the making and the Lowe’s benefit that helped make it possible
summary: An associate’s goal years in the making and the Lowe’s benefit that helped make it possible
body_markdown:
For years, an unfinished chapter lingered in Nikki Brent’s life.


After welcoming her first child, Nikki stepped away from high school and made four determined attempts to return. Each time,


life’s


twists and turns led her elsewhere.


“Life happened, and kids


came


and divorce happened and remarriage happened,” Nikki said. “I had put it down for so long.”


Yet the sense of something left undone never faded.


“I was really down on myself there for a long time because I didn't graduate,” she said. “I really didn't want to hear anybody walking the line. I was jealous. I was super jealous.”


Nearly a decade into her career at Lowe’s, Nikki discovered a benefit she hadn’t realized was within reach: Guild.


So, she decided to try again.


Still, skepticism met Nikki’s first look at Guild, the details almost too good to believe.


“Nobody just offers to pay for things,” she remembered thinking.


As she learned more, this opportunity began to stand apart from all the rest.


“Lowe’s paid for everything when I first started my tuition,” Nikki said. “There was nothing to worry about.”


Nikki is one of a growing number of Lowe’s associates using the company’s tuition-free education program to take the next step. In 2024 alone, more than 800 associates graduated with the program’s support, bringing the total to 1,900 graduates since its launch.


For Nikki, that next step had been waiting for years.


“I


would've


never


got


it done if it wasn't for Guild, and that's my honest opinion,” she said.


Nine months after starting the program, Nikki earned her high school diploma, graduating with a 3.5 GPA.


“Wow,” she remembers thinking. “How did I do that?”


The diploma gave Nikki something she had wanted for years. But earning it also changed how she saw herself.


“It unlocked the part that I could actually get my diploma, my high school diploma, and be proud of myself,” Nikki said.


That newfound confidence began to ripple through other parts of life.


At Lowe’s, Nikki says she approaches projects differently. When she walks into a project now, she tells herself: “I got this. This is


all


me right now. I got this.” Beyond work, new dreams are taking shape. A lifelong love of photography is now blossoming into a budding business.


Once, the question was: “Can I really do this?” Now? “I feel like I could reach the stars,” Nikki said. “I feel anything is possible. I feel that I can do anything that I put my mind to.”


Guild


appeared in Nikki’s life almost by chance. Now, she hopes more Lowe’s associates discover the same opportunity.


“I was on the fence too,” she said. “I had a lot of


anxiety


going back to school. I had a lot of


negativity


going back to school.”


For those standing at the edge of a new beginning, Nikki’s advice is simple:


“You need to do this for you. You need to be proud of yourself. And as I said, just opening it up and looking, you never know what can come out of it.”


For Nikki, everything began with finally earning the diploma that had been out of reach for so long.


What came next was realizing just how much more she might be capable of.
